rows.text: calls `0031B760()` and returns 0 when the result is null, when bit 3 of its dword `+0` is clear, when its qword `+0x698` is null or when byte `+5` of that object is non-zero; otherwise returns the inverse of bit 23 of the dword `+0`

returns 0 when `ecx - 1` is above 0x1D (unsigned); otherwise indexes a byte table after the body by `ecx - 1` and dispatches through a jump table to an arm that returns one of 0x15 to 0x1E, or 0; the byte table's contents are not decoded in the listing
calls `002640C0` with the incoming registers, pops a value with `00267E10(r9)`, resolves `002650B0(002640C0 result, rdx, value)` and tail-jumps `003E92F0(002640C0 result, resolved pointer)`
tail-jumps through the eight-byte entry, indexed by the sign-extended byte `+0x3C` of `rcx`, of the code-pointer table that the `lea` at `00505560+0x5` loads, with the incoming registers

calls `002640C0` with the incoming registers and zeroes three stack floats; when `003590D0()` is non-zero calls `00265020(003588B0(that value), &float0, &float1, &float2)`; then resolves three pointers with `002650B0(002640C0 result, rcx, 00267E10(r9))` in turn and stores float0 through the third, float1 through the second and float2 through the first
pops a value with `00267E10(r9)`, resolves `002650B0(002640C0(), rdx, value)` and tail-jumps `002393E0(rdx, resolved pointer)`
pops a value with `00267E10(r9)`, resolves `002650B0(002640C0(), rdx, value)` and tail-jumps `002395A0(resolved pointer)`

notes: 0030BEB0 is the same row as in derived-call-signatures. 003241D0: the case-to-return mapping depends on the byte table after the body, which the listing does not decode, so the row states only the range of returned values; the jump table and byte table are deliberately not named. 00505560: the pointer table it jumps through is not named, per the rule against naming jump tables; the page itself calls it the type table. In 005105A0/005106D0 the 002640C0 call follows 00267E10, so its rcx is whatever 00267E10 left; written as 002640C0().
